subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should an existing session pinned to an official openai/* model automatically adopt the Codex harness when the Codex plugin becomes enabled, or should it stay on OpenClaw until the user explicitly switches runtime?
rationale: Current docs and code support both pieces of context: OpenAI agent models default to Codex when the harness is available, while /model UI copy says the model switch is session-only and runtime unchanged.

options.title: Preserve session pins, require plugin-only repro
options.body: Keep documented session model pins intact, add a DeepSeek-primary regression, and only change Codex activation if live proof shows plugin enablement alone changes the selected provider.

options.title: Require explicit runtime switch
options.body: Make existing OpenAI-pinned sessions stay on OpenClaw after Codex enablement unless the user selects a Codex runtime, trading surprise reduction for a behavior change from current OpenAI defaults.

options.title: Document current OpenAI behavior
options.body: Treat OpenAI session pins adopting Codex as intended and improve /status, /model, and doctor guidance for users who expected their configured primary to resume.

recommendation.title: Preserve session pins, require plugin-only repro
recommendation.body: Keep documented session model pins intact, add a DeepSeek-primary regression, and only change Codex activation if live proof shows plugin enablement alone changes the selected provider.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history spans Codex harness introduction and selected session model resolution.
